# dotsafe

> A local-first, zero-knowledge secret manager for developers. Secrets are encrypted on your Mac and synced through storage you already own (iCloud Drive, Google Drive, Dropbox, S3 or R2, WebDAV). It ships as a macOS app and a `dotsafe` CLI. AI agents can run commands with secrets through its MCP server without dotsafe ever handing them a value.

Every docs page is plain Markdown at its URL plus `.md`.

## Getting started

- [Introduction](https://dotsafe.dev/docs.md): What dotsafe is and how it keeps your secrets
- [Install](https://dotsafe.dev/docs/install.md): Download the app and the CLI, and activate your license
- [Quick start](https://dotsafe.dev/docs/quick-start.md): Create a vault, import a .env file and run your app

## Guides

- [Projects and environments](https://dotsafe.dev/docs/environments.md): Projects, environments, inheritance and references between variables
- [Secrets and rotation](https://dotsafe.dev/docs/secrets.md): Share one value across environments, rotate it in one step and keep its history
- [Integrations](https://dotsafe.dev/docs/integrations.md): Rotate keys through OpenAI, Cloudflare and AWS, and push them to Vercel and Workers
- [AI agents](https://dotsafe.dev/docs/agents.md): Let Claude Code, Cursor and other agents run commands with secrets they never see
- [Storage and sync](https://dotsafe.dev/docs/storage.md): Keep the vault in a synced folder, an S3 or R2 bucket, or WebDAV
- [Devices](https://dotsafe.dev/docs/devices.md): Touch ID unlock, adding a Mac with a code, and removing a lost device
- [Import and export](https://dotsafe.dev/docs/import-export.md): Bring variables in from .env files and other secret managers, and keep them out of git

## Reference

- [CLI](https://dotsafe.dev/docs/cli.md): Every dotsafe command and its main options
- [Security](https://dotsafe.dev/docs/security.md): How the vault is encrypted, what the app and agents can see, and what dotsafe never stores
